$comment: Illustrative machine-readable CBOM profile for fleet remediation of IoT devices: an operator of a deployed estate deciding, per device model, whether to update it, replace it, put something in front of it, or accept it. It extends the change core, as the PQC migration profile's sibling: a branch, not a depth, because it serves a different decision and asks for facts the migration profile has no use for. The subject is a device model as its manufacturer ships it. What varies per deployed unit is the operator's, held in its own inventory. The worked example is two illustrative LoRaWAN soil sensors, one that can never be updated and one that can.
title: IoT Device Estate (Example)

objective.$comment: C1. Fleet remediation, chosen from three candidate decisions in the IoT use case.
objective.consumer: An operator of a deployed device estate, or an assessor acting for one, that did not build the devices and cannot inspect them.
objective.decision: For each device model in the estate: whether its cryptography can change in place, has to wait for replacement, can be moved behind a gateway, or can be accepted and documented.
decisionOptions: terminate the protected session at a gateway in front of it

scope.$comment: C11. Device models as shipped: subject type 'product', stage 'implemented'. The purposes taken in depth are the change core's.

$commentInterfaceTypes: Devices have four kinds of interface a server does not, and the baseline's interface types cover them without new values: a provisioning or onboarding interface and a firmware update channel are 'management'; a radio link whose cryptography its own standard fixes is 'interconnect'; a telemetry uplink that only sends is 'service'. A device with no management interface states why under the baseline's P2.
$commentUpdateSupport: A commitment class, not a date. 'never-offered' is the value for a model with no update mechanism.
$commentTermination: Where the model's design lets the cryptography of an interface terminate: on the device, at a gateway, or both. A set, because a design can allow both. Whether a deployment does terminate at a gateway is the operator's fact, stated by terminatedBy.
$commentExecutionEnvironment: One location vocabulary is shared by executionEnvironment (where key operations run) and keyStoreLocation (where keys are held), so that a consumer can compare the two on one interface. A value that makes no sense for one of them, such as os-keyring for execution, is simply not used there. A device mostly needs secure-element, mcu-internal and otp-fuses.

overrides.note: Tightened from SHOULD. On a constrained device, integrationConstraints is the attribute that explains the resource bound (P1): whether a post-quantum handshake fits the memory and the link's message size.

productRules.description: Device states the hard limits that bound what any firmware could support
productRules.note: Usable flash, RAM and the largest frame the link allows, in bytes, written 'flash=<n> ram=<n> frame=<n>'. On a constrained device, a 'no' to a capability question is often set by these limits, which no firmware release changes. This is how a permanent 'no' is told apart from a temporary one.

productRules.description: Device states whether the manufacturer will still offer firmware for it
productRules.note: A device in the field outlasts the commitment to ship firmware for it. With updateMechanism (change core P2) and updateAuthority (change core I14), it separates an update the operator can actually make from one that exists only on paper.

interfaceRules.note: Where the key material came from. With keyReplaceable (change core I16), it is the fact that turns an update decision into a replacement decision: factory-injected material that cannot be replaced means the device has to go.

Where the design permits the cryptography of this interface to terminate: 'device', 'gateway', or both. The option of putting something in front of the device depends on it. SHOULD, because it is partly a deployment fact. Renamed from terminationOptions; 'either' is now the two values together.
Where the key operations of the interface execute.

exclusions.reason: Whether a model is safe is a judgement against criteria that change while it sits in the field. The profile states facts; a dated policy reaches the verdict.
Serial numbers, locations, configuration and remaining life are not known to the manufacturer. The operator joins the record to its own inventory.
An SBOM question, reached through the baseline's R1.

Debug ports, bootloaders and readable flash decide whether key material can be extracted, but they are a product security assessment, not a fact about cryptography at an interface. A record can point to such an assessment through the 'code-analysis' or 'platform-assessment' context kinds when they are defined.

exclusions.item: How long the operator will keep a model in the field
exclusions.reason: The operator's planning input. The manufacturer states support (P2); field life is the estate's.

changelog.summary: Initial version, built on two illustrative LoRaWAN soil sensors.
Attribute names made clearer and consistent across the profiles (drafts/attribute-naming-review.md; decision 0028). The version is unchanged because no release has been published.

changes.summary: Renamed: cryptoTerminationPoint → terminationOptions, now a set of 'device' and 'gateway'; 'either' becomes both values. A record that uses the previous name no longer conforms.
Renamed: resourceBound → resourceLimits. A record that uses the previous name no longer conforms.
Renamed: providerLocation → executionEnvironment, with the shared location vocabulary. A record that uses the previous name no longer conforms.
